title: What happens to digital roots when we keep adding eleven?
description: We write any number and keep adding eleven. Eleven is nine plus two, so each step raises the digital root by two, and a root that passes nine comes back round. A check by carrying the list further shows when the roots repeat.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fixed step moves the digital root by a fixed amount round the ring of one to nine, and eleven moves it by two. Watch for students who add eleven to the root itself instead of two.

video_script.why: A learner sees that adding eleven each time moves the digital root by two round the ring of nine.
video_script.substitution: the book's own step, adding 11, from the start number 5
video_script.anchor: a ring of the nine digital roots with the roots of the sequence marked on it
video_script.payoff_line: The digital roots go up by two each time, and all nine appear before they repeat.

final_answer.value: The digital roots go up by 2 each time (after 9, start again), so all nine appear before repeating
final_answer.spoken: the digital roots go up by two each time, and all nine appear before they repeat

hold_back: The digital roots go up by 2 each time (after 9, start again), so all nine appear before repeating
maths_rules: 11 = 9 + 2; adding 9 keeps the digital root; adding 2 raises it by 2, taking away 9 when it passes 9
the roots 5, 7, 9, 2, 4, 6, 8, 1, 3 are all nine roots, and the tenth number 104 has root 5 again
